The model

Text order is for binding; edges are what run

Node
a pure application of a client Operation to argument text. Reads fields, defines fields, produces an output; may unfold children, claim followers, open or close scopes.
Use → reaching def
the nearest earlier visible definition, found in O(log n) from bracket summaries.
Wait
only for that definition's value, or for pending structure the binding walk crosses.
src/lib.rs:3-15 · src/engine.rs:4-18

The model

The four rules

I
Order is used only for binding
Text order decides which definition a use sees, never when anything runs.
II
Nothing waits except on what its binding crosses
A pending node elsewhere in the program blocks nobody.
III
The schedule changes speed, never results
Ids are content hashes; canonical Report counters are schedule-independent.
IV
Evaluation is eager
Every node runs once its bindings are known. No demand counting (removed in 5e969d0).

Consequences: no current state, no stack, no phase that visits nodes in order. A sequential interpreter has all three; that is what makes it the reference, not the model.

The client contract

A client is a set of Operations

pub trait Operation: Send + Sync {
    fn name(&self) -> &'static str { "op" }
    fn defs(&self, args: &[ValueId], values: &Values)
        -> Option>;      // None = pending
    fn may_define(&self, ..) -> MayDefine { MayDefine::Any }
    fn may_define_field(&self, .., f: Field) -> bool { true }
    fn effect(&self, ..) -> Effect { Effect::None }
    fn claim_limit(&self, .., following) -> Option;
    fn claim(&self, .., following) -> Claim { Claim::None }
    fn until(&self, .., cand: OpId, cand_args) -> Until;
    fn until_value(..) -> bool;  fn until_values(..) -> bool;
    fn until_predict(&self, .., following) -> Option;
    fn reads(&self, ..) -> Option> { None } // hint
    fn run(&self, cx: &mut Ctx<'_>) -> Result;
}
HookCalledGives
defs may_define effect claim reads until_predictonce per distinct (op, text), memoizedstructure known from text
runevery time inputs changeoutput, defs, children, dynamic structure
Stop is returned via ? from any Ctx read whose value is not ready; the engine re-runs the operation from the start later. Operations must be pure.
Text-only hook answers are cached in Engine::statics; if something besides the text changes them, the client calls Engine::refresh_where (commit e1ae33a).

Example · cold evaluation

The same program, batch by batch

Rule I. The text says line 5 comes after line 3; nothing makes it run after.
Rule IV. Eager: nobody asked for w; it runs because its binding is known.
With Threads(16) the batches are identical; only the time per batch changes (rule III).

Data · order tree

One augmented treap per unit, keyed by label

fn combine(&self, a: OSum, b: OSum) -> OSum {
    OSum {
        c: a.c + b.c.saturating_sub(a.o),
        o: b.o + a.o.saturating_sub(b.c),
        work: a.work + b.work,
        maxh: a.maxh.max(b.maxh),
        pend: a.pend + b.pend,
        maxr: a.maxr.max(b.maxr),
        maxhit: a.maxhit.max(b.maxhit),
    }
}
Brackets compose like a monoid of )…)(…( shapes: a close in b first cancels an open of a. The depth at a label is just fold(0, label).o.
OItem.hit is reach or 0 while the claimer waits for a recompute: each pending claim is hit once per flush (9b7fc36).

Data · values

Values are content-hashed and interned

pub enum Value {
    Unit, Bool(bool), Int(i64), Str(Box),
    List(Box<[ValueId]>),
    Nil,            // the empty sequence
    Seq(SeqNode),   // canonical treap node
}
fn content_id(v: &Value) -> ValueId {
    // composites hash the ids of their parts
    Value::List(xs) => hash_words(4, &ids(xs)),
    Value::Seq(n) => hash_words(5,
        &[n.left.0, n.elem.0, n.right.0, n.prio]),
}
  • Equal values ⇒ equal ids, in every process; a collision is detected and panics.
  • Values: 64 RwLock shards + a per-thread direct-mapped read cache (4096 slots); a value read twice gets a private copy.
  • Field(ValueId): any value can name a field.

Data · hashing

Two hashers, both deterministic

FxHasher
For internal tables (FxHashMap, FxHashSet). Keys are mostly hashes already. rotate_left(5) ^ w, * K. No random seed, so iteration order is reproducible run to run.
fn add(&mut self, w: u64) {
    self.0 = (self.0.rotate_left(5) ^ w)
        .wrapping_mul(FX_K);
}
hash_words / hash_bytes
Strong mixer (wyhash-style 64×64→128 "mum") for content ids: ValueId, NodeId, child ids, the environment.
Equal environments give identical ids and results (tested).

The loop

evaluate → rounds → drain

The loop

The batch cycle

Level: the lowest non-empty bucket of the height queue. A Done node lower than every queued node is settled; non-speculative runs only read settled values.
Run: run_job(&self, job, fuel) builds a Ctx, does the gate walks, calls op.run. Every read becomes a recorded Use.
Apply: results sorted by NodeId before commit, so the commit order does not depend on which thread finished first.
"At least one ready node always runs" (sanitize): a scheduler cannot stall progress.
src/engine.rs drain, sanitize, run_job

The loop · code

The heart of drain

loop {
    self.flush_claims();
    self.settle_deferred();
    self.flush_order();
    let Some((level, at_level)) = self.queue_first() else { return Ok(()) };
    self.level = level;
    for s in at_level {
        if dirty(s) && has(F_REBIND) && self.revalidate(s) { continue; }
        if dirty(s) { ready.push(s); }
    }
    // speculative candidates: higher levels + parked nodes
    sched.select(&just_ids, &cands, &mut batch);
    Self::sanitize(&ready_ids, &cands, &mut batch);
    {
        let this: &Engine = self;
        exec.execute(batch.len(), &|i| this.run_job(batch[i], fuel), &mut results);
    }
    results.sort_by_key(|r| r.node);
    for r in results.drain(..) { self.apply(r); }
    self.settle_deferred();
}
Claims first. Structure edits queue claimers in claim_dirty; recomputed once per flush.
One level. Nodes dirtied only by re-binding (F_REBIND) are revalidated, which is cheaper than any run.
Policy. Scheduler chooses; sanitize dedups and forces one ready job.
Parallel. A shared &Engine; the Executor decides threads.
Sequential. Deterministic commit order. ~1 s of 1.34 s cold at 16 t.
src/engine.rs drain (condensed; profiling spans and counters removed)

The loop · heights

Heights order work; the queue is a bucket array

Invariant
A Done reader is higher than what it read. So the level is a frontier: everything below it is final.
Critical path
Engine::critical_path(): the dependency depth the heights reached. 17 for the 10k typing program, 44 at 100k (runs below). Steps ≈ number of levels visited: 99 at 10k, 422 at 100k.
Heights are estimates
"It decides when a node is tried, never a result" (child_heights doc).

The loop · gate

The gate: read hints checked before a node starts

fn gate_walks(&self, x: Slot)
    -> Result, End> {
    let n = self.n(x);
    if !n.has(F_HINT) || n.has(F_APP) { return Ok(vec![]); }
    let Some(reads) = self.statics(n.op, n.args).reads.as_ref()
        else { return Ok(vec![]) };
    for &f in reads {
        if self.loop_vals.contains_key(&f) { continue; }
        let w = self.walk(n.unit, n.label, f);
        if w.pending != NIL {
            return Err(End::Gated(w.pending));
        }
        if w.site != NIL {
            let t = self.n(w.site);
            if t.in_work() { return Err(End::Gated(w.site)); }
            if t.height >= self.level {
                return Err(End::GateRaise(t.height + 1));
            }
        }
        walks.push((f, w));
    }
    Ok(walks)
}
The gate runs inside the parallel job (read-only). Its walks are handed to the run, so use_field does not walk the same field again: gate walks were 23% of cold (de5d2a3, 3.16 s → 2.72 s at 1 thread).
Report: gated counts nodes held back. In the 10k run below: 4057 gated of 11256 runs.

The loop · pluggable policy

Scheduler picks, Executor runs

pub trait Scheduler {
    fn speculation_budget(&self) -> usize { 0 }
    fn max_outstanding(&self) -> usize { 4096 }
    fn fuel(&self) -> u64 { 10_000 }
    fn select(&mut self, ready: &[NodeId],
              candidates: &[Candidate], batch: &mut Vec);
}
pub trait Executor {
    fn execute(&mut self, n: usize,
        run: &(dyn Fn(usize) -> RunResult + Sync),
        out: &mut Vec);
}
pub enum Speculation { Off, Predicted, All }
pub struct Candidate {
    pub node: NodeId,
    pub has_prediction: bool, // ran before / F_PREDICT
    pub waiting: bool,        // parked
}
ImplWhereBehaviour
Greedysched.rsall ready; speculate per Speculation, budget/step

Sequentialsched.rsexecutor: jobs in order on the calling thread

The loop · apply

apply(RunResult): the commit, in order

Early cutoff
Readers are dirtied only if the output or a definition's value actually changed. cutoffs counts runs whose output and definitions came out unchanged.
Two-phase apply
Child start heights are computed in the parallel phase (child_heights); the commit adds in-text siblings and binds without walking (bind_fresh) (de5d2a3).
Waking
A parked node sits on exactly one node (on). release_waiters is shared by free_node and make_inert (418470d fixed a missing wake).

Binding · walk

Depth-indexed lookup: one range query per enclosing scope

let mut depth = self.order.fold(&OAug, root, 0, bhi).o;
let mut hi = label;
loop {
    let opener = self.order.search_back(&OAug, root, bhi, &|s| s.o >= 1);
    let lo = opener.unwrap_or(0);
    if let Some(..) = self.local_ix
        .range((unit, f, depth, lo)..(unit, f, depth, hi)).next_back()
    { local = Some(..); break; }
    match opener {
        Some(k) if depth > 0 => {
            bhi = k; hi = (k + 1).min(hi); depth -= 1;
        }
        _ => break,
    }
}
"A local definition reaches the use iff it lies directly in one of the scopes enclosing the use: one range query per enclosing level, never a scan over closed scopes." Unmatched closes at depth 0 are ignored.

Incrementality · stream claims

Stream claims and the touch log

Why a log
A stream claimer's run reads a range of structure, not just fields. Other jobs in the same evaluation can unfold or free nodes in that range after the claimer started; the log lets apply detect that without locking.
Cycle guard
A taken node that reads the claim back never parks: each run feeds the next. STREAM_RUN_LIMIT (4096 runs) per evaluation reports a Cycle.

Harness · benchmarks and the replay client

typing, chains, and JSONL traces

typing.rs
1k / 10k / 100k / 1M-line generated programs: cold, then single-edit replays (insert / delete char, change far def, insert def, redefine meaning, edit in claim, move block close), each checked bytewise against cold unless --no-check. --scaling, --bounded, --trace FILE.
chains.rs
N pending claims in a row, each one's extent known only from the previous claim's result. inert (listuntil) and stream (collect) shapes; three edits checked against the interpreter. SPEC=off|predicted|all.

Harness · profiling build

--features profile: counters, spans, Chrome traces

# release code + full debug info + probes scripts/profile.sh 10000 --edits 5 --no-check # = nc.sh build --profile profiling --features profile \ # --example typing # run.sh target/profiling/examples/typing \ # --trace target/trace.json ... # open target/trace.json in ui.perfetto.dev
  • Without the feature every probe expands to nothing: release pays zero (test probes_count_only_in_profile_builds).
  • Counts and span totals are per thread, merged at thread exit or snapshot: no cross-thread contention in what they measure.
  • On wasm32 spans are counted but not timed (no clock).

The slice
defuse.slice: MemoryMax=32G MemorySwapMax=0 (set with systemctl --user set-property). A runaway run is killed instead of taking the machine (dc76fd8).
Stable too
No nightly-only API in the crate so the cluster's stable rustc builds it (0c7cd92); nc.sh uses nightly locally.
Pedantic allowances
Crate-level #![allow(clippy::many_single_char_names)] (treap code); the rest are local #[allow]s with a reason.

Workflow · commits

What a commit in this repo looks like

Two-phase apply: child heights in the parallel phase; runs reuse the gate's walks ← subject: the mechanisms, ';'-separated A run's result now carries the starting height of each child it will unfold (...); the commit adds in-text siblings and binds without walking (bind_fresh). The gate's walks are handed to the run, so use_field does not walk the same field again in the same job. ← body: what changed and why typing 100k cold: 1 thread 3.16s -> 2.72s (the run side: gate walks were 23% of cold and re-walked by use_field); 16 threads 1.43s -> 1.37s. The sequential apply itself barely moved (998 -> 984 ms at 16 threads): what remains in it is index mutation (...), not walks. ← numbers, before -> after
One concern per commit, and the honest negative: "the sequential apply itself barely moved".
Numbers from the same benchmark and size, before and after, with the thread count.

Open problems

Where to look next

1
Sequential apply
~0.98 s of 1.34 s cold at 16 threads. What remains is index mutation: order-tree inserts, local_ix/global_ix/defs_ix/users updates (de5d2a3). Ideas need to keep the commit order deterministic (results sorted by NodeId).
look at: apply, set_children, set_uses, add_def, bind_fresh
2
Speculation storms on pending-claim chains
Each link's extent depends on the previous claim's result, so a chain resolves one claim per step. The symptom to look for is mispredictions growing with the chain length when speculation is on (not measured for this deck). chains.rs measures it (SPEC=off|predicted|all).
look at: recompute_claim, refute_assumers, Report.mispredictions
3
Deep-unfold traces start nodes too early
Reported for traces with deep unfolding: nodes are started many times before their inputs are ready (each start ends in a Stop; watch stops vs runs). Not reproduced for this deck. Child heights from read hints (child_heights) help only where the trace gives hints.
look at: child_heights, gate_walks, End::Raise, Report.stops / gated

Keep the four rules
If a change makes a result depend on the schedule, the random scheduler and the fuzz will find it. If a change waits on something the binding does not cross, pending_waits will show it.
Ask the oracle
When in doubt about semantics, the interpreter is the definition; the engine must match it bytewise.
